previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted with sepsis from a gangrenous right foot ulcer. She initially underwent a below-knee amputation, but due to poor wound perfusion, an above-knee amputation was required. She was treated with IV imipenem for multidrug-resistant Proteus mirabilis and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Her dialysis access was transitioned from the femoral vein to a tunneled external jugular catheter to reduce infection risk. Warfarin was held perioperatively and bridged with heparin, with plans to resume outpatient anticoagulation. She developed emotional distress post-amputation, which improved with counseling support. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation, ongoing heparin bridging until INR therapeutic, and follow-up with vascular surgery.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with gangrene
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Infection with drug-resistant microorganisms, unspecified, with multiple drug resistance
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ is very ___ to the Vascular surgery service 
given her extensive peripheral vascular disease. She is most 
recently s/p above-knee amputation on the right side in ___ 
and presented to clinic for a wound dehiscence with malodorous 
drainage. The patient was admitted, received IV antibiotics, and 
underwent multiple bedside debridements with exposure of 
sufficient healthy granulation tissue to allow for 
vac-placement. The patient tolerated these debridements well. 

Neuro: the patient received Dilaudid PO with good effect and 
adequate pain control. 

CV: The patient was stable from a cardiovascular standpoint; 
vital signs were routinely monitored. She has a history of 
atrial tachycardia, and was continued on her home dose of 
amiodarone without issue. 

Pulmonary: The patient was stable from a pulmonary standpoint; 
vital signs were routinely monitored.

GI/GU: the patient has ESRD and is HD dependent. Her schedule 
was continued throughout her course, with her last HD session on 
___, which she tolerated. Her electrolytes were monitored on 
a routine basis. She was placed on a cardiac/diabetic/renal 
diet, which she tolerated well. She was also started on a bowel 
regimen to encourage bowel movement.

Intake and output were closely monitored. 

ID: The patient presented with a dehiscence of her stump site; 
given her previous history of proteus and klebsiella in her 
wound cultures, she was started on imipenem as an outpatient. 
This was continued upon admission. ID consult was obtained given 
the patient's complicated history, with recommendations to 
continue the impenem and await deeper wound cultures, which 
similarly grew proteus as well as enterococcus, which was 
sensitive to daptomycin. Daptomycin was then started on ___ 
prior to discharge; both antibiotics were to be continued for 
___ weeks until follow-up on ___ with ID.  The 
patient otherwise remained afebrile, with twice daily dressing 
changes prior to switching to a vacuum-assisted device. 

Endo: the patient has a history of diabetes, which was well 
controlled with a regular insulin regimen.

Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin during 
this stay for DVT prophylaxis, and received daily dosing of 
coumadin for known history of bilateral IJ thromboses.

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
with stable vital signs, tolerating a regular diet, voiding 
without assistance, and pain was well controlled.

She was discharged on a course of Daptomycin 8 mg/kg q48h and 
Imipenem 250 mg q12h for ___ weeks with a follow up/update visit 
with ID on ___. In addition, because of decreased

Discharge Instructions:
This information is designed as a guideline to assist you in a 
speedy recovery from your surgery. Please follow these 
guidelines unless your physician has specifically instructed you 

otherwise. Please call our office nurse if you have any 
questions. Dial 911 if you have any medical emergency.
.
ACTIVITY: 
.
There are restrictions on activity. On the side of your 
amputation you are non weight bearing until cleared by your 
Surgeon. You should keep this amputation site elevated when ever 

possible. 
.
You may use the other leg to assist in transferring and pivots. 
But try not to exert to much pressure on the amputation site 
when transferring and or pivoting.

No driving until cleared by your Surgeon.
.
PLEASE CALL US IMMEDIATELY FOR ANY OF THE FOLLOWING PROBLEMS: 
.
Redness in or drainage from your leg wound(s) .
.
Watch for signs and symptoms of infection. These are: a fever 
greater than 101 degrees, chills, increased redness, or pus 
draining from the incision site. If you experience any of these 
or bleeding at the incision site, CALL THE DOCTOR. 
.
Exercise:
.
Limit strenuous activity for 6 weeks. 
.
Do not drive a car unless cleared by your Surgeon. 
.
Try to keep leg elevated when able.
.
BATHING/SHOWERING: 
.

WOUND CARE:

Please have wet-to-dry dressing changes performed twice a day 
until your follow up with your vascular surgeon, Dr. 
___. 
 
.
When the staples are removed the doctor may or may not place 
pieces of tape called steri-strips over the incision. These will 

stay on about a week and you may shower with them on. If these 
do not fall off after 10 days, you may peel them off with warm 
water and soap in the shower. 
.
Avoid taking a tub bath, swimming, or soaking in a hot tub for 
four weeks after surgery.
